# Model providers

Veasel ships 84 provider presets in the V binary. This count describes endpoint presets, not independent SDKs or equivalent feature coverage. Four protocol adapters currently power them: OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, and Google Gemini. The 36 entries sourced from Models.dev use Veasel's shared OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions transport; provider-specific SDK features, authentication schemes, and model capabilities are not implied. The OpenAI Responses preset and Meta Model API use the Responses transport. OpenAI reasoning parameters are sent only for reasoning-capable model families; Meta uses high reasoning with automatic summaries and stateless encrypted reasoning replay for tool loops.

The TUI fetches this catalog from the local Veasel server. Press s on the home screen or use /models in a session to search providers. Settings collects the endpoint and credential before model discovery, then checks the provider's model-list endpoint and lets you choose a returned ID or enter one manually. A newly entered key is sent to the local server in a POST body for discovery and is saved only when you choose a model. Discovery does not create a profile, issue a model prompt, or start generation. Credentials can also come from the listed environment variable or an existing saved profile.

Models.dev entries are selected from [anomalyco/models.dev](https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev), an MIT-licensed community-maintained catalog used by OpenCode. Veasel pins the source revision to [7e111b466a9c677234fb22d311b9e0bae795d84b](https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/tree/7e111b466a9c677234fb22d311b9e0bae795d84b); the selected base URLs, credential variable names, and documentation links are checked into tools/provider-catalog/providers.json. The V source and this page are generated from that file. No Models.dev network request, Node runtime, or other provider package is needed by Veasel after compilation. HTTPS provider requests validate server certificates against the operating system CA bundle; set SSL_CERT_FILE to use a custom PEM bundle. Windows uses the system certificate store.

The Models.dev selection filter requires its OpenAI-compatible adapter marker, an HTTPS API base URL, exactly one credential variable, and no unresolved URL template. Presets are not live-availability guarantees; endpoint access, account eligibility, model IDs, regional settings, and tool support depend on each provider. The openai-compatible preset remains available for custom endpoints. Local presets target loopback by default. Meta's live model discovery lists the models enabled for the configured Model API account; the documented coding choices include Muse Wonder 1.0 and Muse Spark 1.3. Veasel currently sends text and tool schemas and caps each model response at 4,096 output tokens.

If live model discovery fails, Veasel reports safe upstream status details without returning the provider response body or submitted credential. HTTP 401 means the provider rejected the key; 403 means the account or model lacks access; 404 usually means the configured endpoint has no model-list route, so enter a model ID manually; 429 means the provider rate-limited the request. Other failures keep a generic message to avoid exposing provider response data.
